Invariant

Board Design Proof Findings

AI Psychosis maxxing

We were told to touch grass. Instead we built twenty-seven 3D pictures of our own research.

Every picture is drawn from the team's real data, no vibes-only renders. Agents built one idea each, fully locked in. These are prototypes: they run best on a desktop with a graphics card.

  1. 01

    Our results, crystal-maxxed

    One crystal for each result on the board, grown by a stated rule. The healing-crystal shop on Valencia could never.

    Board, live
  2. 02

    Inside the model's head, literally

    The 32 layers, the directions RL changed in each matrix, and the loop neurons behind answers that repeat themselves forever.

    Weight readouts
  3. 03

    Finish the thought or hit the cap

    Each stored answer falls by its token count and either finishes or gets cut off at the cap mid-yap.

    Rows per answer
  4. 04

    Weight arithmetic on a dial

    Every model made by adding weight changes together, with a dial over how hard the edit is sent. No thoughts, just vectors.

    Stored readouts
  5. 05

    Every problem is a bead

    One bead for each problem slides between right and wrong as the configuration changes. You can watch the vibe shift.

    Rows per problem
  6. 06

    Number go up, in plaster

    Every posted score of one benchmark as a plaster relief, with the best so far as a thread. The hill we climb, rendered as an actual hill.

    Scores, live
  7. 07

    Called it (or did we)

    Each theory's forecasts, locked in before the numbers were measured, against what landed. Receipts, not vibes.

    Theory rounds
  8. 08

    The grind, as a spiral

    Items, messages, commits, GPU jobs and scores at their real times, one turn for each hour. Sleep does not appear.

    Board, git, jobs
  9. 09

    Repo city

    One block for each file, as tall as its line count, replayed commit by commit. Builds faster than anything SF has permitted.

    Git history
  10. 10

    Who cited whom

    Which board item cites which, regrown from the first hour. The family tree of every take.

    Board references
  11. 11

    What the agents do all day

    Each agent session as a wire, each tool call as a bead, each subagent as a branch. Proof they were locked in.

    One laptop's transcripts
  12. 12

    The board, but throwable

    Every board item as a rigid body to grab, throw and sort. For when the to-do list deserves to be yeeted.

    Board, live
  13. 13

    The whole thing in one take

    Ninety seconds, one camera move, 500 brass pins: the plain base, the opening cue, the vote, the weight edit and RL, each counted on the same problems. No cuts, we are not cowards.

    Rows per problem
  14. 14

    The studies, in clockwork

    A brass orrery: one arm for each study, set as far from the gilt RL sphere as its best base-model score is short of it, one bead for each result. Turn the crank through 25 hours.

    Board, git
  15. 15

    The hill climb, as a race game

    A baize race board with one brass token for each method family, moved only when a better MATH-500 score was posted. RL is a fixed post. A bell rings when a token passes it.

    Scores, live
  16. 16

    The Invariant Gazette

    A letterpress front page for every three hours of the hackathon, set only from what was posted on the board in that block. All the news that fits a token cap.

    Board, git
  17. 17

    Two days, woven

    A floor loom where every commit is one row of the cloth and every band of warp is an area of the repository. The stripes show which study had the floor.

    Git log
  18. 18

    500 drawers, 12 that never open

    A card catalogue with one drawer for each MATH-500 problem. The tags flip when you change the configuration, and every drawer holds the problem on an index card with what each model answered.

    Rows per problem
  19. 19

    Who called whom

    A telephone exchange where every direct message between agents is a patch cord. Most calls stay inside one person's own panel: the agents mostly talk to themselves.

    Messages, board
  20. 20

    The hackathon on chart paper

    A five-pen chart recorder tracing board items, messages, commits, GPU jobs and open work for 30 hours, and still writing live. Drag the paper to pull time back.

    Board, git, live
  21. 21

    Democracy, for samples

    Four samples of each problem drop as balls into a ballot cabinet and the tallest stack wins. Pull the lever and watch the vote fix what one sample got wrong.

    Rows per sample
  22. 22

    Rising tide, 500 stones

    One stone for each MATH-500 problem, easiest to hardest, flooded to the level each configuration reaches. The islands are the problems that break the order.

    Rows per problem
  23. 23

    Call the number

    A game: set your forecast on a slide rule before the measured number is shown, scored by the same rule as the team's theories. Humbling, in a healthy way.

    Theory forecasts
  24. 24

    The hackathon, as a music box

    Every commit, board item, message and score is a pin on a brass cylinder that plucks a steel comb. Turn the crank to hear two days of work. Sound on.

    Board, git
  25. 25

    Who is carrying what

    A hanging mobile balanced by real physics: one leaf for each open work item, live. It leans toward whoever holds the most. You can blow on it.

    Board, live
  26. 26

    What a point costs

    A brass balance that weighs each method's tokens per problem against the accuracy points it bought, next to RL's price.

    Scores, live
  27. 27

    The reading list, shelved

    One book for each paper the agents read before running anything. Pull one out and it opens on the findings recorded from it. Yes, they did the reading.

    Paper records
